title: PolicyArtifact
description:
A policy artifact: a whole program, which runs in place of the default program.

An artifact is typically derived by editing the export of the default program. It is complete: every node after the host's sources is the artifact's, and nothing of the default program runs beside it. It records nothing of what it was written against.

Artifact nodes have local identifiers: composing the artifact into a plan assigns their plan IDs. Artifact edges refer to the host's sources as `input.<name>`, by the `binding` of their `source` nodes. Artifacts refer to configuration by binding only, never with resolved values, and may write any parameter value as a reference to a blob in their blob table, which composition replaces with the blob's content (see [`Blobs::inline`]).

Serializing an artifact writes its normalized form, as for a [plan](Plan#normalized-form). Approval binds to the hash of the document as it was received, which [`ReceivedArtifact`] keeps.

blobs.description: Content-addressed values that parameters refer to.

edges.description: The edges between the host's sources and the artifact's node ports.

ir_version.description: The IR version the artifact is written in.

ArtifactEdge.description: An edge within a policy artifact.

from.description: The port the edge leaves: a source, or an output port of an artifact node.

to.description: The port the edge enters: an input port of an artifact node.

ArtifactNode.description: One node of a policy artifact.

op.description: The registered operator the node runs.

ArtifactPortRef.description: A port reference within a policy artifact: `input.<name>` (one of the host's sources, only as an edge's source), or `<node>.<port>`.

Params.description: Operator parameters, keyed by parameter name. Each operator's parameter schema defines their types.
